ladder.what: 12 V input power of the whole card
ladder.gran: 10 mW; a new value every service-processor pass: about every 156 ms on aifoundry2, 158 ms on aifoundry1-c1 and 263 ms on aifoundry3 while ettelem samples (the SP trace's own pass: 160, 162 and 266 ms under the sampler, 133, 135 and 224 ms with no sampler running; §4.1)
ladder.instrument: DM_CMD_GET_MODULE_POWER, or the SP stats trace
ladder.note: The host can poll much faster than the value changes (ettelem's six-command sample takes 22 ms), but the service processor refreshes once per loop pass. The PMIC (a closed ATSAMD20 firmware) does the averaging. Some workloads starve the SP and slow the reading, on aifoundry2 to about two new values a second; on 23 September aifoundry3's sampler kept its pace in the same bursts, but in the version-3 campaign's reruns the same ring starved the sampler on all three cards (§4.1).

ladder.what: Minion cores, SRAM (L2/L3/scratchpad arrays), NoC
ladder.gran: 1 mW; the PMIC's running average (τ ≈ {{rf_tau}} s) of each regulator's output power, copied by the SP every pass (156–263 ms by card while ettelem samples, §4.1); min and max since the last reset, which restarts the average too
ladder.note: The output side (w_out) of the three PMBus regulators only; the other rails have no power telemetry, and the input side is read by the SP but not forwarded (§4.1). ettelem --reset-ms reads the min/max over a chosen window (in every pass on aifoundry2 and aifoundry3; on aifoundry1-c1 one pass of three saw the maximum fall once with no reset), and each reset restarts the running average: with a reset every second, a rail had fallen 93% of the way one second after a burst, on all three cards (§4.1).

ladder.what: pJ per L1/L2/L3/DRAM load, per FMA slot
ladder.gran: ≥ 10⁹ identical events/s for 3 s bursts bracketed by idle; bars ±7% (median) over passes and cards
ladder.instrument: regression of rail power against counted events
ladder.note: Bursts bracketed by idle, with the burst's own warming corrected and bursts off 600 MHz discarded, three passes on each of three cards (rung 1); the chart at the end of this section shows which events this method can price, against one reading's step of about 156 µJ on a rail (aifoundry2 while ettelem samples).

ladder.what: DDR, L2/L3, PCIe DMA bandwidth and core utilisation
ladder.gran: 1 ms samples, chip-wide
ladder.note: The master minion's statistics worker (MMST trace) stops and restarts every shire-cache and memory-shire counter every 1 ms.

ladder.what: 35 temperature sensors, 125 voltage sense points (3 per minion shire, 2 per memory shire, IO and PCIe shires), 35 process detectors
ladder.gran: hardware 0.06 °C (12-bit) / 75 µV (14-bit); host sees 34-shire avg/low/high at 1 °C / 1 mV every SP pass (156–263 ms by card while ettelem samples, §4.1)
ladder.note: Per-shire voltages work now (DEBUG trace): they leak out as DEBUG log strings through DM_CMD_SET_DM_TRACE_CONFIG (the per-shire voltage map in Power and temperature, §3); per-shire temperature needs a firmware change; the process detectors are configured with measurement disabled and never read; two external analog VM inputs have a stub reader and no caller. No sensor measures current (§4.3).

ladder.what: The 0.8 V memory-shire supply as the Moortec monitors in the 8 memory shires see it, 1 mV, every SP pass
ladder.gran: {{droop_slopes}} mV per watt of off-rail DRAM power on {{cards}}, each fitted over {{droop_ns}} configuration means (rms {{droop_rmss}} mV): 1 mV ≈ {{droop_mvw_cards}} W
ladder.note: Calibrated against the §4.2 regression, so not independent of the board meter; heavy mesh, scratchpad and L3 traffic moves it too (§4.3).

ladder.what: The part of board power on no rail sensor, split into delivery losses of the metered rails and a per-byte DRAM cost
ladder.gran: rms {{fit_rmss}} W over {{fit_ns}} configuration means on {{cards}} in that order ({{fit_rmsd}} W on the DRAM ones); coefficients ±{{se_minion}} (minion), ±{{se_dram}} (DRAM), ±{{se_noc_sram}} (NoC, SRAM)
ladder.instrument: regression of (board − rails) against rail powers and DRAM bytes (§4)
ladder.note: Not a sensor: an attribution. It cannot say how the DRAM term splits between the DDR PHY, the I/O rail and the DRAM chips, nor how the idle {{idle_unsensed}} splits between DDR, PCIe, the IO shire and the regulators' own draw.

ladder.what: v_in, a_in, w_in and a_out of the minion, SRAM and NoC regulators
ladder.gran: 1 mW class, per SP record (every pass), already read by the SP
ladder.instrument: PMIC PMBus statistics (pmic_get_pmb_stats) forwarded by a new SP stats field
ladder.note: Would turn the fitted {{minion_pct}} delivery loss of §4 into a measurement per rail and per load, and shrink the unmetered remainder to the rails that truly have no meter.

ladder.what: Correctable/uncorrectable errors in shire-cache SRAM and I-cache; DRAM and PCIe counters
ladder.gran: per event; which 64-bit doubleword of a line, not which bit
ladder.note: Wired but dark: DRAM ECC is compiled off, and the SP never enables the PLIC sources for SRAM/I-cache errors, so those counts stay 0. L1D, tensor scratchpad and register files have no ECC or parity at all.

ladder.what: Retired instructions per thread, L1D misses, I-cache requests/misses
ladder.gran: per launch, summed over a neighbourhood of 8 minions
ladder.note: Events are fixed at boot; mhpmevent is M-mode. 32 minion and 25 neighbourhood events exist in the RTL, bit-exact with the PRM table.

ladder.what: Minion clock cycles, free-running
ladder.gran: 1 cycle (1.67 ns at 600 MHz)
ladder.note: Two counters per neighbourhood, not synchronised across neighbourhoods; a read just after the low 7 bits wrap comes back 128 short, on all three cards, but the short window is not a fixed length: fixcyc() (Anatomy of a memory access §7), which corrects reads whose low bits are below 11, left 0–4.7% of intervals off by 128 in a launch (§3), so check corrected intervals for ±128 outliers. The standard cycle, time and instret CSRs trap.

ladder.what: Load-to-use latency of one load after placing its line in L1/L2/L3/DRAM
ladder.gran: 1 cycle, one load
ladder.note: This is how the memory-anatomy report split a DRAM load into cache, mesh, controller and row-state parts to ±3 cycles for 97% of lines, on aifoundry2.

ladder.what: Software events with a cycle stamp: strings, values, PMC snapshots, profile regions
ladder.gran: 1-cycle stamp; ~20–40 cycles per entry (estimate)
ladder.note: A sink, not a new resolution. scripts/trace-flamegraph.py now turns profile events into per-hart flame graphs in cycles (workloads/traceprof, one run on aifoundry2 on 20 September: 512 events from 32 harts in 2.6 ms of kernel time, 1.57 M cycles). Stamps come from the neighbourhood's even- or odd-hart hpmcounter3, each reset separately at boot, so they compare only between harts sharing a counter.

ladder.what: Per-bank reads/writes/cycles; per-memshire NoC reads/writes at 933 MHz
ladder.gran: one 40-bit counter per syscall (hundreds of cycles); chip-wide
ladder.note: Only the boot-time qualifiers. The memory-shire monitor can count DRAM activates, precharges and refreshes per bank, and the shire cache can measure queue occupancy (mean miss latency by Little's law), but selecting those needs M-mode.

ladder.what: L1 access/miss per thread, L2 miss rejections, tensor waits; L2/L3 hit/miss and occupancy; DRAM command counts
ladder.gran: same counters, any event
ladder.instrument: a new U-mode syscall writing mhpmevent / sc_perfmon / ddrc_perfmon
ladder.note: Written and verified in the simulator: patches/0003 adds a U-mode syscall (about 60 lines in four files), and workloads/pmcsel shows hpmcounter6 switching to a chosen event with the rebuilt firmware. Running it on the card needs a signed image.

ladder.what: GPRs, PC, seven CSRs, 8-byte memory words of a halted hart; hardware PC breakpoint
ladder.gran: 64 bits per management round trip (ms); halt unit = one neighbourhood (16 harts)
ladder.note: In every shipped BL2 variant and the node is 0666, but dev_mngt_service refuses the commands: a ~100-line libDM client is needed. Hazards: a halted worker wedges its kernel, RESET_HART is a stub, the debug clock is gated at boot. Rehearse on sys_emu first.

ladder.what: One instruction per resume of a halted hart
ladder.gran: 1 instruction per ms-scale round trip
ladder.note: The ENABLE_SINGLE_STEP command is a stub, but dcsr is writable by raw address. Erratum 1.18: safe only for harts 0/1 of a neighbourhood. Untested here.

ladder.what: Trap on any instruction matching a mask, log state, resume
ladder.gran: 1 instruction, hundreds of cycles of perturbation
ladder.note: A software single-step or a tensor-op logger without the debugger. PRM §14.1's 0x1C cause is a typo for 30.

ladder.what: Read or write one 128-bit quadword of L2/L3/scratchpad with its check bits
ladder.gran: one quadword per M-mode transaction
ladder.note: The closest thing to reading a stored bit on silicon, and a deliberate bit-flip injector (write with wrong ECC, read through the normal path).

ladder.what: Run one shire at a different clock to attribute the minion rail's power to it
ladder.gran: per shire, 25 MHz steps; ~0.3 W resolvable against a 1 mW LSB
ladder.instrument: per-shire LVDPLL and clock mux ESRs via SP firmware
ladder.note: The mux and PLL exist per shire, but the shipped firmware puts every shire on the chip-wide step clock, and erratum 7.3 calls the LVDPLL unstable on A0.

ladder.what: Instantaneous rather than averaged rail power, 10–50× faster loop
ladder.gran: tens to a few hundred Hz
ladder.instrument: SP firmware: drop the 84-read PMB snapshot, fix the 1 ms I2C busy-wait
ladder.note: The values are already read and discarded each pass. External: a scope on the LTC4218 IMON pin gives board total at ~kHz.

ladder.what: Every instruction with every register, lane, mask, memory and CSR write
ladder.gran: per instruction; no cycles, no cache contents
ladder.note: The same emulator is the golden model the RTL was verified against. The README's 'Fetched instruction' line is stale; the real line is I(prv): pc (bits) disasm.

ladder.what: Instruction trace per cycle, 128 selected signals per neighbourhood, 200 memory-controller signals
ladder.gran: per cycle, selected signals
ladder.instrument: UltraSoC status monitors and trace encoders over JTAG/USB
ladder.note: Real logic on the die; the IP, protocol and Data Book are not open, nothing configures it, and boot clock-gates it.

ladder.what: Full flop state of a shire via scan chains
ladder.gran: one dump, clock stopped, state destroyed
ladder.note: Designed in, with errata on the chain routers; no ATPG patterns or chain descriptions are open.

ladder.what: Every net, flop and SRAM bit of one neighbourhood (8 minions, VPUs, L1, I-cache) per clock
ladder.gran: 1 simulated cycle; toggle counts per signal
ladder.note: Verilator 5.042 now builds here without root, and single open-RTL modules simulate with waveforms (rtl-sim/pmu_carry runs neigh_pmu.v and explains a silicon bug; rtl-sim/fma_toggle counts the multiply-add flips behind the Horace experiment). The full 8-minion bench still needs its missing verilator.mk and cosim library; the main branch's whole-minion co-simulation references original files that are not in the public drop. No shire cache, NoC or DRAM; no cell library, so no joules.

ladder.level: Individual bit toggling on the fabricated chip
ladder.what: Watching one node switch in real time
ladder.note: The honest boundary. Everything above it is the answer.

contrast.et: Every instruction's 32-bit encoding is in the PRM; objdump names the custom CSRs; kernels are plain ELF.
contrast.gpu: PTX is documented; SASS is opcode names only. Encodings and control bits were reverse-engineered by third parties.
contrast.src: PRM §2.4; NVIDIA CUDA Binary Utilities; Jia et al. 2018

contrast.et: 13 design documents (541 pages) plus the RTL: pipeline stages, miss handlers, VPU latencies, PMU implementation.
contrast.gpu: Whitepapers and tuning guides; latencies and cache geometry come from microbenchmark papers.
contrast.src: core-et/docs; NVIDIA whitepapers; Luo et al. 2024

contrast.et: hpmcounter3 per neighbourhood, 1 cycle, with a documented (here) carry bug whose window is not fixed (§3).
contrast.gpu: clock64() per SM, 1 cycle; %globaltimer counts in 32 ns steps but updates about once a microsecond (NVIDIA forum; the PTX manual gives no resolution).
contrast.src: this report; CUDA Programming Guide; NVIDIA developer forum

contrast.et: Fixed neighbourhood events in U-mode; per-bank cache and per-memshire counters by syscall; events selectable with a firmware change.
contrast.gpu: Nsight/CUPTI per-SM, per-L2-slice, per-FBPA aggregates; PC sampling; no per-bank/row or per-request data.

contrast.et: PA bits → L3 home shire, memory shire, bank, row, column, from the PRM and firmware, confirmed by counters.
contrast.gpu: L2 hash and DRAM bank/row mapping undocumented; recovered by timing (GPUHammer 2025).

contrast.et: Board power at 10 mW, a new value every service-processor pass: about every 156 ms on aifoundry2, 158 ms on aifoundry1-c1 and 263 ms on aifoundry3 while ettelem samples (133, 135 and 224 ms with no sampler running, the SP trace's own pass), plus three rails as the PMIC's ~1 s running average at 1 mW; no energy counter.
contrast.gpu: One board number: a 25 ms average every 100 ms on A100/H100; a mJ energy counter; no rails.
contrast.src: NVML docs; Yang et al. SC'24; this project's power-telemetry notes

contrast.et: L2/L3/I-cache SECDED with error logs (dark at this firmware); no L1D or register ECC; DRAM ECC off.
contrast.gpu: ECC on register file, L1, L2, HBM; counts per location, no syndrome or bit position.
contrast.src: PRM Tables 15-77 and 15-81; NVIDIA Memory Error Management r575

contrast.et: MDI: halt, breakpoint, GPR/CSR/memory of a hart, via the service processor; no gdb server for silicon (sys_emu has one).
contrast.gpu: cuda-gdb: breakpoints, warp single-step, register reads; no watchpoints.

contrast.et: Service processor and minion runtime are source; images are signed, key not open.
contrast.gpu: GSP firmware is a signed binary; user-mode driver closed.

contrast.et: Functional emulator with per-instruction state; RTL of the core with waveform dumps and lockstep cosim.
contrast.gpu: None. Accel-Sim is a tuned performance model driven by SASS traces.

reports.title: Limits of observability (this page)
reports.what: The hub: every instrument on the card, what it resolves, what it cannot see, the unmetered power attributed, and the ladder of improvements; since 26 September, the version-3 campaign on three cards and every page's claims before and after it.
v3_note: failed their registered test (10 in something the page says, now corrected; 2 only in a number it does not quote)

reports.title: Heat per millimetre
reports.what: The energy of moving one bit one millimetre across the mesh, with the data on the links chosen: per bit that differs from the previous flit, per one carried, and the part no data changes, on contended and uncontended links, against Dally's ~100 fJ/bit·mm.
reports.instruments: board power, NoC rail, die temperature, the sampler's latency; the die plot for millimetres per hop

reports.title: The energy manual
reports.what: Energy per instruction, per byte at every level, per message, per atomic, with confidence bars from repeated passes on three cards; the idle law; wires, lines, rows, leakage of the arrays, rails; since 27 September gathers, scatters and packed atomics by level (E48, three cards: a random 4 B element 12.8 pJ from the L1, 354 pJ from the L2, 9.8 nJ from DRAM).
reports.instruments: board power, rails, die temperature, cycle counter; the leakage law

reports.title: The DVFS loop and its leakage
reports.what: The governor's states and thresholds and the three operating points (aifoundry2; aifoundry3's firmware runs with a TDP of 0 W, which a lab service sets at every boot, so that card never leaves 600 MHz); the idle law on aifoundry2: idle power rises about 0.65 W per °C near 80 °C, and 20–29 W of the 36 W idle at 80 °C is leakage (a fixed part plus an exponential fits equally for e-folding lengths of 30 to 45 °C, so the split is a range; one session: the three-card check got no long idle pass to confirm it); the rail split of idle, the activity term; the open RTL's per-minion sleep controls are tied off, and the wake-up probe showed no array power gating (one probe on aifoundry2; since 26 September three on each of the three cards).
reports.instruments: board power, rails, SP trace, DM_CMD config reads, driver ioctl

reports.title: The Horace experiment
reports.what: Same matmul, same FLOPs: 38 W on zeros, 47 on ones, 63 on random data (aifoundry2; the same order on aifoundry3 and aifoundry1-c1: in the three-card check, four runs each, ones added 8–9 W over zeros on every card and random data 24–27 W); on aifoundry2, RTL flip counts predict the power of 14 patterns to 0.5 W rms (leave-one-out) and priced 14 structured matrices before they ran; a flips-to-temperature model; the power model carries to a second card with one scale factor (0.92 on 22 September). In the three-card check aifoundry3 switched 0.895 of aifoundry2 over the eight patterns (least squares; the model's own scale for it 0.88) as registered, but 0.958–0.969 with busy and idle power compared at the same die temperature (the registered values compare them at a fixed reference, which puts a per-card offset in them: AMENDMENTS C2), close to the catalogue's independent 0.972, and aifoundry1-c1 1.004 of it (registered 1.009); whether aifoundry3's remaining few per cent is the card or its cooler die the check could not tell. A demonstration, one morning on aifoundry2 (seven runs): from a cool die, zeros ran 25% faster than random data.
reports.instruments: board power, die temperature, RTL simulation of the multiply-add unit

reports.title: Why is the ET-SoC-1 low power?
reports.what: Esperanto's P = C·V²·f + leakage measured term by term through ablations at 80 °C on aifoundry2 and set against an A100: voltage and clock give 5–6× less switching power; 1,024 cores in an integer loop add 1.5 W on aifoundry2 (four runs in the three-card check; on aifoundry3, +0.4 W, and aifoundry1-c1, +0.7 W, the loop is not distinguishable from idle as registered; with busy and idle power compared at the same die temperature, AMENDMENTS C2, it is 0.8–1.6, 1.3–1.9 and 0.0–0.8 W on the three cards, the range set by the launch reading's whole degree; the energy manual's catalogue gives 1.9–2.0 W for a one-hart addi loop on the three cards); about 20–29 W of the 36 W idle at 80 °C is leakage (one session; not confirmed by the three-card check); and per FLOP the card still spends more energy than the A100's bf16 tensor cores.
reports.instruments: board power, rails, preheated strict starts

reports.title: Power and temperature telemetry
reports.what: The first look at the meters: every way to read power, voltage and temperature and what each resolves; board power refreshed once per service-processor pass, every 156–263 ms by card while ettelem samples (the hub, §4.1), three rails behind the PMIC's ~1 s average; idle power that rises with die temperature; the 34-shire voltage map from the SP's DEBUG trace (aifoundry2, one idle capture; not confirmed by the three-card check, which got too few complete idle captures).
reports.instruments: board power, rails, die temperature, SP stats and DEBUG traces

reports.title: Hand it to the next shire
reports.what: A multi-stage relay: handing each stage's output to the next shire runs 12× faster than a round trip through DRAM, at about a thirteenth of the energy per byte (13× on each of the three cards), and keeping it in the shire's own scratchpad about 31× faster; which shire receives the slab changed bandwidth by up to a quarter over all 31 ring offsets (592–741 GB/s; three passes on each of three cards, two where aifoundry3 lost a launch; the next shire by ID is 1–10 mesh hops away, 3.5 on average; what each hop costs in energy is in Heat per millimetre).

reports.title: One hot line stops a shire
reports.what: One contended global atomic: every shire, the host included, gets its fair share (0.998–1.004) at one atomic per 10 cycles, while, at a steady 600 MHz, the host shire's own loads fall to 0.02% of normal; about 20 nJ per contended atomic, 17× a spread one.
reports.instruments: cycle counter, per-minion completion counts, board power

reports.title: Anatomy of a memory access
reports.what: On aifoundry2: one load taken apart to ±3 cycles for 97% of lines: the L3 home shire from PA[10:6], the memory shire from PA[8:6], DRAM banks, rows and refresh, and where the eight memory shires sit around the mesh; energy per load split by rail (since re-measured in the energy manual); the cycle counter's late-carry bug and its fix.
reports.instruments: evict_va + cycle counter, memory-shire read counters (syscall 10), board power, SP rail trace

reports.title: Memory hierarchy
reports.what: Latency, bandwidth and capacity of every level, next to the A100: L1 8.8 ns, L2 78 ns, L3 ~280 ns and DRAM ~490 ns at 600 MHz, the same on all three cards (three passes each in the three-card check; first measured on aifoundry2), and 76 GB/s streaming (aifoundry2). Its energy per byte now comes from the energy manual §4 (since 26 September six passes on each of three cards: L2 3.1, L3 14.7 and DRAM 115 pJ/B pooled, the L2 and L3 moving from 1.4 to 5.0 and from 7 to 21 pJ/B pass to pass), which superseded the page's own 18 September figures. Since 27 September, gathers and scatters by level on the three cards (E48): past the L1 every element fetches its own 64 B line, 27.4 G elements/s from the L2 and 1.19 G/s from DRAM.
reports.instruments: cycle counter, board power polled through dev_mngt_service

reports.title: On-chip communication
reports.what: Where the 32 shires sit on the 6×6 mesh: a round trip costs 150 cycles plus 12 per mesh hop, the same on all three cards (three passes each in the three-card check), and a hop takes 20 ns at any clock (aifoundry2); TensorSend/Recv, credits, barriers, reduction trees and rings: cycles per message, a 2.3 µs chip-wide allreduce (1,393 cycles, the same on all three cards), 7–34× less bandwidth between shires than inside one (aifoundry2), and pJ per byte (re-measured in the energy manual §5).
v3_note: held with no difference between the cards

reports.title: Matmul efficiency
reports.what: A tensor-unit matmul loop on cached tiles, all 1,024 minions: 9.5 TFLOP/s fp32, 19.0 fp16 and 71.8 TOP/s int8 (91–97% of peak), the same to 0.1% on all three cards (four passes each in the three-card check, every launch bit-exact; first one session on aifoundry2), board power under load (aifoundry2) and a spec-sheet comparison with the A100; also the first hello world on a card. Its operands are ±1 and ±2; the Horace experiment later showed that random data draws more power. (The scalar SGEMM is in Test drive.)

reports.title: Ridge points
reports.what: Peak compute divided by each level's bandwidth: the operations per byte a kernel must do before compute, not memory, sets its speed. In fp32, 4 per byte from its own shire, 10 from L3 or another shire, 130 from DRAM (fp16 twice that, int8 eight times); what that takes for blocked matmul and for batch sizes; the limits that act like ridge points; energy balance points from the energy manual's measurements.
reports.instruments: none: arithmetic on the 18 Sep reports' data and the energy manual's

reports.title: Test drive
reports.what: First contact: the toolchain built on a Mac, hello worlds on the sys_emu simulator, a scalar fp32 SGEMM (127 GFLOP/s on 2,048 harts, no SIMD or tensor unit: first one session on aifoundry3, and the same on all three cards in the three-card check, three passes each), and three upstream issues found on the way.

reports.title: Influence functions on the ET-SoC-1
reports.what: Exploratory, estimates from the measured numbers: which steps of large-scale influence-function work suit the chip. None of a big lab's bill does; two narrow research items survive, the stronger (S1) scoring a small fixed index held in on-chip SRAM a few queries at a time, and one card experiment would settle it. The gather/scatter measurement it asked for (S3) was made on three cards on 26 September: a scatter-add passes 10 G updates a second only while its buckets stay inside a shire.
reports.instruments: none: desk analysis of the set's measurements

reports.title: Sparse compute
reports.what: What the tensor unit does with zeros, first on aifoundry3: zero-skip saves power but never a cycle (in a TensorFMA loop on small integers, all-zero data draws 86%, 93% and 92% less power over idle than dense data on aifoundry2, aifoundry3 and aifoundry1-c1 as registered, three runs each, and 86–90%, 86–88% and 91–96% with busy and idle power compared at the same die temperature, over AMENDMENTS C2's two readings of the launch temperature); masked loads and skipped empty slices take a batch-1 1024×4096 fp32 layer held in SRAM from 7.5 to 2.1 µs at 99% zeros, the same on all three cards (2.4 and 2.6 µs for two other random patterns of 99% zeros); narrow lanes against divergence; six scenarios where the chip could beat an A100. Its power result is the one the Horace experiment later resolved into flips.
reports.instruments: cycle counter, board power polled through dev_mngt_service

reports.title: Spatial temperature: a brief
reports.what: The 35 Moortec temperature sensors on the 6×6 grid of minion, I/O and PCIe shires, the firmware's reduction to one whole-degree average, and the firmware changes a spatial heat map would need; the peak-hold high shows how far the hottest shire ran above the average each time it rose (2 or 3 °C at every rise on all three cards in the three-card check, 3 at 61–83% of the rises; 2–4 °C, mostly 3, in the earlier logs of aifoundry2 and aifoundry3), never which shire.
reports.instruments: firmware (353f20e) and RTL (b38a1a3) source reading; the committed ettelem logs of both cards

reports.title: L2 mainline starvation (superseded)
reports.what: An argument from Ivan's report, written before the reproduction; now a pointer: see One hot line stops a shire (the owner's share of the atomic is 1.004, not 6%; what stops is its other memory traffic). The TensorSend layouts it warned about are in On-chip communication.
reports.instruments: none: the spec, the errata and a reported result

droop.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-25-claims-v3/raw/aifoundry2/catfull/p*/telemetry.jsonl.gz (die_mv from DM_CMD_GET_ASIC_VOLTAGE: the Moortec voltage monitors averaged over the 8 memory shires for ddr, the 34 minion shires for minion/sram/noc); computed by tools/ettelem/fit_unmetered.py

host_sees.voltage: minion-shire average of VDD_MNN, VDD_SRAM, VDD_NOC; memory-shire average of VDD_MS (as 'ddr'); IO shire VDD_MXN and VDD_0P75; PShire VDD_PSHR; the PMIC set points (integer mV)
host_sees.debug_trace: per-shire VDD_MNN/SRAM/NOC lines every loop pass at LOG_LEVEL_DEBUG (all 34 shires captured on each of the three cards); the per-memory-shire lines (MEM n Voltage) appeared in the three-card check only in captures taken right after a telemetry sample
host_sees.not_exported: per-shire temperature, process detectors, external analog VM inputs

rail_filter.rule: minion rail over idle > 8 W, >= 4 s idle each side; fall after the board's step-down, relative to the idle before the burst; median over bursts; tau fitted over 0.1-3 s

checks.source: tools/ettelem/sync_hub_data.py checks(), with fit_unmetered.py's config_means, _fit and droop on catalogue.json and each card's catalogue telemetry (catalogue_telemetry(): the V3-CATFULL blocks, raw/<card>/catfull/p*/telemetry.jsonl.gz)

improvements.group: software, on the data the card already gives
improvements.what: Bracketed bursts with a leakage correction and a clock-excursion filter
improvements.cost: done (energy manual, 23 Sep)
improvements.effect: Confidence bars of ±7% (median) on 392 entries, three passes on each of three cards since 26 September; the first reruns on aifoundry2, started from a cool die, whose bursts spent 5–25% of their samples at 700–800 MHz, were caught by the filter and discarded (aifoundry3 never leaves 600 MHz).

improvements.group: software, on the data the card already gives
improvements.what: Attribute the unmetered remainder by regression
improvements.cost: done (this page)
improvements.effect: Unmetered power above idle named per configuration: {{minion_pct}} delivery loss on the minion rail, {{dram_pj}} pJ per DRAM byte off-rail (§4.2). The idle {{idle_unsensed}} stays unattributed.

improvements.group: software, on the data the card already gives
improvements.what: Read the DDR rail's droop as a DRAM-power proxy
improvements.cost: done (this page); calibration is the regression of rung 2
improvements.effect: DRAM activity every SP pass at 1 mV ≈ {{droop_mvw_cards}} W on the three cards, confounded by heavy mesh, scratchpad and L3 traffic; a second witness for the DRAM term.

improvements.group: software, on the data the card already gives
improvements.what: Undo the rails' one-second average
improvements.adds: The PMIC's rail averages, as the SP forwards them, are roughly first-order ({{rf_1s}} of a step at 1 s, {{rf_2s}} at 2 s; τ ≈ {{rf_tau}} s, measured on the catalogue's bursts with no reset; a reset restarts the average, §4.1). Inverting that filter sample by sample recovers rail power every refresh (§4.1).
improvements.cost: ~50 lines in the analysis scripts; a calibration burst to pin τ
improvements.effect: Rail split of bursts shorter than 3 s; per-launch rail energy; the minion/SRAM/NoC split of transients.

improvements.group: software, on the data the card already gives
improvements.what: Per-shire current maps from the DEBUG trace's IR drop
improvements.adds: The SP prints every minion shire's VDD_MNN/SRAM/NOC voltage each loop pass at LOG_LEVEL_DEBUG (the map in Power and temperature, §3). Calibrate each shire's drop against the rail meter with single-shire loads, and the map becomes current.
improvements.cost: a day: single-shire calibration bursts, a trace parser (sptrace exists)
improvements.effect: Where the metered watts go on the die, per shire, to about 10%; the spatial power map that the temperature sensors cannot give from the host.

improvements.group: software, on the data the card already gives
improvements.what: Sub-degree temperature by step timing; min/max windows for peaks
improvements.adds: The integer die reading steps at sharp moments when polled at 10–45 Hz; fitting the heating that reproduces the steps gives rises that repeat to ±0.03 °C on aifoundry2 and about 0.2 °C on aifoundry3 for a pattern heating the die by a degree or more (the Horace experiment); below about one degree it only bounds the rise. ettelem --reset-ms reads the PMIC's min/max over a window (in every pass on aifoundry2 and aifoundry3; on aifoundry1-c1 one pass of three saw the maximum fall once with no reset), and restarts the rails' running average with each reset.
improvements.cost: done
improvements.effect: Thermal responses without a firmware change; peak power over any window.

improvements.group: software, on the data the card already gives
improvements.what: Watch the meter itself: its latency, and its queue
improvements.adds: Every ettelem sample records how long its six management commands took (took_ms); bursts during which the SP is starved (a median over 60 ms) are dropped from the reruns and the heat-per-millimetre runs (§4.1). ettelem exits cleanly on SIGTERM, and the runners drain a poisoned management queue and retry.
improvements.cost: done (23–24 Sep)
improvements.effect: One ring configuration (s ↔ s+16) and one column placement on aifoundry2 are unmeasurable this way (the ring read 33–45% low on aifoundry2 without the check; in the version-3 campaign it starved the sampler on all three cards); DRAM reads slow the sampler too, on aifoundry2 and aifoundry3 (§4.1). After the drain, the second heat-per-mm run (one run per card, 24 September) completed 132 bursts per card with no sampler restart.

improvements.group: lab hardware, no firmware
improvements.what: A PCIe riser with shunts on 12 V and 3.3 V, read at a kilohertz
improvements.adds: An external meter of the card's input, 1 mW at 1 ms, that owes nothing to the PMIC's closed firmware and its refresh of a few times a second.
improvements.cost: a riser or interposer with sense resistors and an INA-class ADC, or a bench DAQ; a day; a slot in an open chassis
improvements.effect: The launch transients that widen the small-signal bars become visible and separable; 0.5 s bursts become measurable; the widest bars (the hot line's −15/+19%, the remote scratchpad's −19/+22% on random data) narrow toward the 1–2% pass-to-pass scatter on one card, leaving the difference between cards; the awake core's bars are −6/+10% (a nop) and the DRAM relay's −10/+16%, mostly aifoundry1-c1 against the other two; the PMIC's own input-power reading gets an independent check.

improvements.group: lab hardware, no firmware
improvements.what: An infrared camera over the open card
improvements.adds: Which packages warm under which load: the DRAM chips, the DDR PHY side of the die, each regulator, the PCIe switch.
improvements.cost: a thermal camera and an open chassis; an afternoon
improvements.effect: The unmetered watts placed on the board: the split of the DRAM term between the PHY, the I/O rail and the chips, and of the idle {{idle_unsensed}} between DDR, PCIe and the regulators, at least in proportion.

improvements.group: lab hardware, no firmware
improvements.what: A second and a third card
improvements.adds: aifoundry3 repeated the catalogue (not its DRAM-row runs), the reruns and the Horace protocol; since 26 September aifoundry1-c1 (older firmware, 1.2.0) joins both in the version-3 campaign, which ran the whole catalogue, DRAM rows included, on all three cards.
improvements.cost: done
improvements.effect: The factor between cards over the whole catalogue, re-run on the three cards: aifoundry3 over aifoundry2 0.976 pass by pass (99% interval 0.961–0.990) and 0.972 as the median over its entries (0.95 in the 23 September catalogue), and aifoundry1-c1 over aifoundry2 0.967 (0.950–0.985; median 0.962). Part of it is temperature, not the card: over a 30-configuration panel of the catalogue, a card read 0.48% higher per °C of die temperature on aifoundry2 and 0.30% on aifoundry3. On the tensor unit's switching (the Horace patterns) aifoundry3 read 0.895 of aifoundry2 as registered, but 0.958–0.969 with busy and idle power compared at the same die temperature (AMENDMENTS C2), in line with the catalogue's 0.972, and aifoundry1-c1 1.004 (registered 1.009); the Horace factor of 0.92 (22 September) could not be separated into card and temperature.

improvements.group: firmware (a signed build; see the firmware caveat)
improvements.what: Forward the PMIC's input-side readings for the three metered rails
improvements.cost: a few lines in the SP stats structure, and a firmware image
improvements.effect: The delivery loss measured per rail and per load instead of fitted; the unmetered remainder shrinks to the rails that have no meter at all.

improvements.group: firmware (a signed build; see the firmware caveat)
improvements.what: Export the 35 temperature sensors per shire
improvements.adds: The spatial brief's three options: a trace field, a DM command, or a DEBUG log line like the voltage one.
improvements.cost: a few lines; a firmware image
improvements.effect: Heat maps on the 6×6 mesh (0.06 °C only if the raw 12-bit codes are exported; the driver's own values are whole degrees); heat flow between shires; per-shire leakage from the idle law.

improvements.group: firmware (a signed build; see the firmware caveat)
improvements.what: Enable the process detectors and the two external analog monitor inputs
improvements.adds: 35 ring-oscillator process detectors (one per minion shire and the IO shire) are configured with measurement disabled and never read; two external analog channels of the voltage monitors have a stub reader and no caller.
improvements.cost: driver already written; a firmware image; for the external inputs, finding what the board wires to them
improvements.effect: Per-shire silicon speed and a leakage proxy that separates the card factor into process and voltage; possibly two board-level sense points.

improvements.group: firmware (a signed build; see the firmware caveat)
improvements.what: Faster, unaveraged power in the SP trace
improvements.adds: Drop the 84-read snapshot and the 1 ms I2C busy-wait; record the PMIC's instantaneous power rather than its average.
improvements.cost: a firmware image; the PMIC's own refresh rate is the next unknown
improvements.effect: Board and rail power at whatever rate the PMIC itself updates (unknown), without the one-second average.

improvements.group: firmware (a signed build; see the firmware caveat)
improvements.what: Enable the SRAM ECC interrupt sources (and DRAM ECC)
improvements.cost: a firmware image, and a decision on DRAM capacity
improvements.effect: Bit errors become observable at the doubleword; the only bit-level detectors the silicon has.

improvements.group: firmware (a signed build; see the firmware caveat)
improvements.what: A U-mode syscall to choose counter events
improvements.cost: written and verified in sys_emu (patches/0003); a signed firmware image
improvements.effect: Per-shire and per-neighbourhood event counts under a workload, instead of the fixed five.

improvements.group: tooling against existing interfaces
improvements.what: A libDM client for the Minion Debug Interface
improvements.adds: Rehearse on sys_emu, which models the debug module. Also writes mhpmevent before a launch, choosing counter events without a firmware change.
improvements.cost: ~100 lines of C++ against /opt/et/lib/libDM; the in-tree gtests are complete examples; a quiet card and a reset plan agreed with the lab admin
improvements.effect: Architectural state of a hart on silicon.

improvements.group: tooling against existing interfaces
improvements.what: Verilator flow for the whole core-et bench
improvements.cost: days of build repair
improvements.effect: Below-silicon views of anything the card measures.

improvements.group: research
improvements.what: A cell library and netlist for the RTL
improvements.adds: Toggle counts from the RTL bench become joules only with a library the drop does not contain.
improvements.cost: not in the open tree
improvements.effect: Energy per flip from simulation rather than from fits to board power.

improvements.group: research
improvements.what: Current sensing below the regulators
improvements.adds: Nothing on the die or the board measures the current of the DDR, VDDQ, PCIe, IO or Maxion rails; splitting them means shunts on the board.
improvements.cost: board rework: not for a shared card
improvements.effect: The last {{idle_unsensed}} of idle, and the DRAM term's split, stay inferred.

sessions.instruments: cycle counter; board power

sessions.instruments: board power, die temperature, DM config reads, SP trace

sessions.instruments: board power bracketed by idle, rails, die temperature, cycle counter

sessions.what: The reruns for the bars: relay, hot line, rings and levels, three warm passes on aifoundry2 and three or four on aifoundry3; the governor and the starved-meter traps found
sessions.instruments: as above; the sampler's own latency

sessions.what: Heat per millimetre, first set: 1 KB tensor loads from a scratchpad d = 0–6 hops away with the bits on the links chosen (bit density P, alternating blocks, single-axis pairs), 82 configurations × 3 passes; a second starved-meter case found

sessions.instruments: cycle counter, board power, rails, die temperature and clock (ettelem), SP stats and DEBUG traces, memory-shire counters
